name: lolcrab
desc: Make your console colorful, with OpenSimplex noise
why: Generates OpenSimplex noise as colourful terminal output, a real generative idea though it leans toward pretty output.

brief.what_it_is: lolcrab is a command-line filter that colorizes text using OpenSimplex noise. It reads files or standard input and writes the same text back out with each character colored by a noise field mapped onto a gradient. Options pick the gradient (rainbow by default, plus presets such as viridis, inferno and turbo, or a custom CSS-style gradient), the noise scale, a seed, inverted background coloring, and an animation mode. It is also a Rust library crate with a Lolcrab type that colorizes strings into any writer.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a more colorful successor to lolcat: "Like lolcat but with noise and more colorful." It is a fork of lcat-rs, and the author describes it as "make your life more colorful, still boring but more colorful".
brief.how_it_works: Each character position is sampled from a seeded OpenSimplex noise field, and the sampled value selects a color from the chosen gradient. The noise scale (default 0.034, suggested range 0.01 to 0.2) controls how quickly colors change across the text. Animation mode shifts the noise over time, and the library exposes methods such as set_invert, randomize_position and reset_position to change the pattern between renders.

commands_seen.context: Installs the lolcrab binary from crates.io using cargo; the README's only install path besides the release binaries.
Prints the location of the config file. The config file holds default flags, one per line, such as --gradient fruits.

brief.install_notes: Pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows are on the GitHub releases page. Otherwise install with cargo, which needs a Rust toolchain. Optional defaults can go in a config file whose path is printed by lolcrab --config-file. No accounts or extra runtimes are mentioned.
brief.standout: It turns OpenSimplex noise into a text-coloring effect, where lolcat uses a plain rainbow sweep. It also ships as both a CLI and a Rust library with a documented example that colorizes a block of text. Its own scout note says it leans toward decorative output, and the README agrees: the goal is looks rather than information.
brief.status: unknown. The README has CI and crates.io/docs.rs badges, and repology packaging info, but it shows no release dates, commit dates or changelog. The library snippet mentions version 0.4. I did not check the releases or commit history.
brief.caveats: The README's config example uses --linear and --spread, which are not in the usage listing, so the docs may have drifted from the code. The library snippet writes default-features = "false" as a string where a boolean is expected. The README also has a typo, "avaliable". It is a fork of lcat-rs, and the README does not state a license. Windows is listed as a binary target, but nothing else about platform support is documented.
